When a customer goes over their limit, the API returns **HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests)** and rejects the request [1]. The response includes a **`Retry-After` header** that gives the number of seconds to wait before retrying [1].

**How it works:**
- Limits are set per workspace, not per API key. Ten keys in one workspace share one budget [1].
- Short bursts up to 2x the limit are allowed for 10 seconds [1].
- Rejected requests don't count against the monthly event quota [1].
- Limits vary by plan and endpoint. For example, event ingest on Enterprise is 10,000 req/s by default [1].

**How customers know when to retry:**
- The `Retry-After` header tells them how many seconds to wait [1].
- Northwind's SDKs read that header and back off automatically, with exponential backoff [1].
- The sources I found don't say what a raw HTTP client should do beyond reading `Retry-After`, so customers calling the API directly will need to handle it themselves.

**Related cases:**
- If an endpoint isn't included in the customer's plan, the API returns HTTP 403, not 429 [1].
- Enterprise customers can get ingest limits raised up to 3x the default by contract, through the account team and the Data Plane queue [1].
- For a one-off backfill, the Data Plane on-call primary can grant a temporary raise of up to 72 hours [1].

A normal change to Ledger needs sign-off from the Identity & Billing change approver, **Harriet Vance**, or her delegate, **Arjun Mehta** [4][1]. Both are out November 24–27 [2], so neither is likely to be available on November 25. If both are unavailable, the policy lets the **VP Engineering, Dmitri Sokolov**, approve [1][4]. Exceptions are logged in `#eng-changes` [1].

**Other checks:**

- **Head of Security sign-off:** Not required by the Restricted-service rule. Ledger is classified Confidential, not Restricted [3]. Restricted covers customer event payloads, credentials and encryption keys [7]. Ledger stores invoices, plan history, usage totals and payment-provider customer tokens [3].
- **Month-end billing freeze:** No normal changes to Ledger apply from the last business day of the month until invoices are sent, usually the 2nd [1]. The last business day of November 2026 appears to be Monday, November 30, so November 25 falls outside that window. This is my own date calculation, not something stated in the sources. The October freeze began on Friday, October 30, which fits the same pattern [2].
- **Holiday freeze:** Starts December 18, so it does not affect November 25 [1].

**What's missing:** The knowledge base has no confirmation of who is actually available on November 25. The only availability information is the October 26 status note [2]. It also doesn't mention any Ledger-specific freeze schedule change for that date. Before relying on the VP Engineering route, confirm with Harriet and Arjun, or with Dmitri Sokolov directly.

You stop trying the ordering clinician after 30 minutes and escalate to the on-call medical director. The result has to reach the ordering clinician within 60 minutes overall. If the clinician can't be reached within 30 minutes, the result goes to the medical director on call [1].

For Wednesday, November 18, the on-call medical director is Dr. Luis Carvalho, with Dr. Ingrid Solberg as backup. That shift runs from Monday, November 16 at 08:00 to Monday, November 23 at 08:00 Eastern [3]. The Thanksgiving swap doesn't affect this date [3].

To page the on-call medical director, call the Halcyon answering service at 555-0144 and choose option 2. If there is no callback within 10 minutes, the service pages the backup. Don't text physicians' personal mobile numbers, because pages through the answering service are logged and timed, which the chart documentation needs [3].

Document each notification in the chart with the time and the person notified [1].

Based on the only quarterly report available, four languages missed their connect-time target in Q3 2026 (July 1 – September 30), which is the most recent completed quarter. Two of these are on the 2-minute tier and two on the 5-minute tier:

- **Vietnamese** (2-minute tier): average connect 2:26 [1]
- **Arabic** (2-minute tier): average connect 2:12 [1]
- **Somali** (5-minute tier): average connect 5:40 [1]
- **Karen** (5-minute tier): average connect 6:18 [1]

The other languages in the report averaged within their targets. The "All other languages (61)" group averaged 3:31 against the 5-minute target [1].

**What the sources don't settle:**

- **Average vs. per-session:** The report gives targets of 2 and 5 minutes and shows averages, but never says whether the target is judged on the average or on individual sessions. I compared the averages, since that is the only figure reported per language. If the target applies per session, more languages could have missed it, and the report doesn't show per-session data [1][2].
- **Quarter:** The Q3 2026 report is the first quarterly report in this format. Earlier quarters were reported monthly by Polyglen and aren't restated, so I found no comparable data for other quarters [1].
- **Next step:** Clinical Operations plans to raise every language that missed its target at the Polyglen renewal discussion in November 2026 [1]. Haitian Creole and Karen are also proposed for the 2-minute tier [2]. Haitian Creole averaged 3:54 in Q3, so it would not have met the 2-minute target either [1].

The Meridian EHR (Wren) cutover is planned for **Saturday, February 6, 2027, starting at 22:00 Eastern, with 6 hours of planned downtime** [2]. The cutover must be finished by 04:00 Sunday so Harbor Point's clinic, which opens at 10:00, has time for verification [2]. The 04:00 end time matches the 22:00 start plus 6 hours.

**The November 18, 2026 date does not change the Meridian cutover.** The CSCAB minutes place "Release on November 18, 2026" under the Wren item, but the surrounding text describes a different change: identifier mismatches held for manual review and holds reported to QPS [2]. That matches Heron, the positive patient identification check before lab results reach the patient portal, which the register lists as "Build complete; awaiting release" with a Q4 2026 target [1]. The minutes also set a December 2, 2026 action to report Heron holds to QPS [2]. So November 18 most likely refers to Heron, not the Meridian upgrade. The sources don't state this outright, so confirm with the CSCAB chair or the project lead, Grace Oyelaran.

**Status and remaining checkpoints for Wren:**
- The February 6, 2027 plan was approved on October 28, 2026 [2]. The register still lists the project as in integrated testing with a Q1 2027 target [1].
- Switchyard interfaces to all reference labs must be retested by January 15, 2027 [2].
- The final go/no-go is at CSCAB on January 27, 2027 [2].
- Meridian Clinical Systems staffs a live bridge line with its own engineers for the whole cutover window [3].
- All clinics will use paper downtime procedures during the window [2].

**What the sources don't cover:** Nothing states the cutover's end time beyond the 6-hour window and the 04:00 Sunday deadline. They also don't say whether the February 6 date could still move before the January 27 go/no-go.

The knowledge base does not give a self-pay price for the RSV vaccine, and it doesn't say whether Halcyon stocks it.

The in-clinic vaccine and injectable formulary (2026–27) does not list RSV at all. - Self-pay prices for vaccines and injectables include the administration fee [1].

- Self-pay patients who have no insurance coverage for a service should receive a good-faith estimate at least one business day before it, or three business days if it is scheduled 10 or more days out [2].

To get the RSV price, check with the pharmacy and therapeutics lead, Dr. Farah Qureshi, or the billing team. I would also confirm whether RSV is on the formulary before quoting a patient.

Yes. Halcyon pairs every new clinical hire with a preceptor, and that pairing lasts 90 days [1]. The preceptor is the equivalent of Northwind's onboarding buddy, though the Halcyon document describes it as a supervision and sign-off role rather than a peer buddy.

**Northwind (duplicate invoices, INC-2340):** The main fix was an idempotency key on invoice creation, scoped to each workspace and billing period. It shipped October 8 [2][3][6]. Before the fix, the month-end job re-ran after a payment-provider webhook timed out, and invoice creation wasn't idempotent [3]. Northwind also added a daily reconciliation report comparing invoices to charges, which is marked done [6].

The retry and webhook side is not fixed yet. The alert for provider webhook timeouts during a billing batch is still open, due November 6 [6]. I found no record of changes to the retry logic itself.

The INC-2340 postmortem is not in the knowledge base. The incident log says it was published October 13 [4], but its text wasn't found, so I can't confirm whether it lists changes beyond those above.

**Halcyon (duplicate medication reminders, IR-0412):** The cause was a September 2 scheduler cutover to a new job runner. Both the old and new runners were active, and neither checked whether a reminder had already been sent [1]. Halcyon made three changes [1]:

- Each reminder now carries an idempotency key (patient, medication, scheduled time), and a reminder with an existing key is never sent again [1].
- Scheduler cutovers require a written runbook and clinical safety sign-off [1].
- Reminder messages now tell patients, "If you already took this dose, you don't need to take it again" [1].

The Halcyon review doesn't describe a retry or webhook change, because that wasn't the cause.
